title: How Indian courts actually apply the polluter pays principle
p1:
A company pollutes a river. Can it simply pay a small fine and move on?

Many people think the polluter pays principle means paying a penalty after causing environmental damage. But Indian courts have applied this idea much more strictly.
p2:
The surprising part: courts do not treat it as just a punishment. The principle means the person or company responsible for pollution must bear the complete cost of repairing the damage, restoring the environment, and compensating affected people.

In cases involving industries, mining, and hazardous activities, Indian courts have used this principle to make polluters accountable beyond ordinary fines.
p3:
The practical lesson is simple: environmental responsibility is not only about following rules before damage happens. It is also about taking financial responsibility when harm is caused.

For businesses, this means compliance is not just a legal requirement; it is a risk management decision. A cheaper shortcut today can create a much larger liability tomorrow.
conclusion: Do you think companies causing environmental damage should only pay fines, or should they be required to fully restore the harm they create?
